article.author: Valerii Karpov
article.dek: Three screenshots exposed a visual experience that a desktop review—and passing layout tests—had missed.
article.evidence: A first-person account in the VKV Studio build log records three screenshots from the author’s own phone and the fixes made to the homepage, assistant mark and log spacing.
article.facts: A first-person account in the VKV Studio build log records three screenshots from the author’s own phone and the fixes made to the homepage, assistant mark and log spacing.
article.interpretation:
The account describes a calmer surface behind mobile text, a plain image replacing the runtime-drawn mark, and removal of unnecessary top spacing. An earlier code change had been overridden by a later CSS rule; another phone review exposed the remaining problem.

A developer’s test result and a reader’s experience answer different questions. Keep both in acceptance: repeat the relevant code checks, then inspect the actual page on the target device. A screenshot should name its URL, date, browser and viewport.
article.limits: This is an internal author account, not a usability study or conversion measurement. The source does not attach the phone/browser configuration, a repeatable device matrix or raw before-and-after evidence.
article.mediaRights: The 48 section scenes and paired Studio workbench are documented staged generated illustrations, not factual photographs or test screenshots. Provenance/rights evidence for the original article covers, OG derivatives, logo and remaining shipped artwork is incomplete. This content-only export records that unresolved state; it is not a media-rights certification or public release approval.
article.practicalDecision: ACT: read the opening, navigation, one article and the contact path on a real phone before accepting a site. Passing desktop layout tests is only one part of that review.

sections.heading: Three screenshots changed the priority list
paragraphs: The author’s August 16 build log records three mobile problems: text competing with the hero video, an assistant mark failing to draw, and empty space inherited from a desktop layout. The desktop view had hidden their combined effect on the opening and reading path.

These observations concern the author’s own site. They do not establish how many customers encountered a problem or how much revenue it cost. They do identify a useful buyer question: what does the delivered site actually let a phone visitor read and do?

sections.heading: A useful review question
paragraphs: ACT for a site with a strong visual opening, a mobile enquiry path or long reading pages. Open the first screen, follow the menu, read an article and reach the contact options on a real phone. Check that the brand and offer remain visible and that the next step can be reached without guessing.

PASS on extrapolating this account into a conversion claim. Agree the intended devices and acceptance cases with the supplier; record unresolved problems rather than treating one successful phone as universal coverage.
